info.description: Self-hosted package registry — app REST API and system endpoints.

parameters.description: Only events at or after this time (RFC3339, inclusive).

parameters.description: Only events before this time (RFC3339, exclusive).

parameters.name: cursor

200.description: Orgs by slug, archived ones included

400.description: Malformed cursor

get.summary: The effective runtime settings (secrets excluded — S-26).

patch.summary: Updates runtime settings: durable write, local reload, cross-instance invalidation.

200.description: Settings after the write, with the new version

400.description: No sections supplied, or a value the validator refuses

get.summary: Instance counters, storage, the supply-chain registers, and job state.
The user table, newest account first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring of the email or display name.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

post.summary: Suspends an account: sign-in is refused and every live session is revoked (S-09).

200.description: Account suspended and its sessions revoked

400.description: An administrator cannot suspend their own account

post.summary: Reinstates a suspended account.
Revokes the current session (S-09): DB truth plus immediate KV blocklist.

Finishes an OIDC flow: single-use state, server-side code exchange (confidential client
+ PKCE), full id_token validation, S-02 linking policy, S-31 domain gate.
post.description: Every authentication failure is the same 401 — the reason lives in the audit log only.

post.summary:
Starts an OIDC flow: state/nonce/PKCE are minted and stored server-side under the
returned `flow_id` (S-01); the browser navigates to `authorize_url`.
Requests an email OTP.
post.description:
The response is uniform whether the email is known, unknown, or rejected by instance
policy (S-04/S-31): always `200 {pending_id}` — rejected addresses simply never receive
mail, and only the audit log knows why. Rate limits: 5/h/email + 20/h/IP → 429 with
`Retry-After` (S-24).

post.summary:
Redeems an OTP for a session (access + refresh pair) — or, when the account has an
active TOTP second factor, for a pending-MFA handle (`mfa_required = true`, S-05).
post.description:
Every failure — wrong code, expired record, unknown pending id — answers with the same
`invalid_code` 401 (S-03/S-04); a code survives at most 5 wrong attempts.

get.summary: Lists the configured OIDC providers for the login screen (public, no secrets).

200.description: Configured providers; empty = email OTP only

post.summary: Rotates a refresh token into a fresh pair (S-08).
post.description:
Reuse of a rotated-out token answers 401 with the distinct `refresh_reused` code — the
whole session family is already revoked at that point.

post.summary:
Marks the current session step-up-fresh after a live second-factor check (S-06 "sudo
mode"). Accounts without TOTP re-authenticate by signing in again instead.

400.description: No second factor enrolled

delete.summary:
Disables the second factor (TOTP + remaining recovery codes). **Step-up required**
(S-06): a stolen stale session must not be able to strip the account's MFA.

403.description: step_up_required — verify a fresh second factor first

post.summary:
Activates the pending enrollment with a live code and returns the ten single-use
recovery codes — the only time they are ever visible (S-05).

200.description: Second factor active; recovery codes shown once

400.description: No enrollment in progress

post.summary:
Starts a TOTP enrollment: returns the base32 seed and `otpauth://` URL. Nothing is
active until `confirm` proves the authenticator works (S-05).

Completes a pending-MFA login (S-05): the `mfa_token` from the first-factor response
plus exactly one of a TOTP code or a recovery code. ≤5 failures per pending attempt,
then exponential backoff (429 + `Retry-After`).

get.summary: The live event stream.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Replay events newer than this id from the instance's short ring buffer (best-effort)

200.description: Server-Sent Events. Each message carries `id:` (an event id, usable as Last-Event-ID), `event:` (the dot-namespaced type) and `data:` (a StreamEvent document). Comment lines (`:heartbeat`) are keep-alives.

401.description: Missing, invalid, or revoked access token

get.summary: Landing/dashboard payload.

200.description: Instance identity, counters, and package rails

post.summary: Accepts an invitation as the signed-in user.
post.description:
Not org-scoped and not step-up gated: the caller is the *invitee*, the token is the
authorization, and the repository additionally binds acceptance to the invited address in
verified state. Accepting is a pure grant, so it does **not** revoke the caller's sessions
(S-09.a) — logging somebody out of every device the moment they join would be a cost with
no security benefit.

403.description: The invitation is bound to a different verified email

get.summary: The caller's notification feed, newest first, with the unread count.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

200.description: Notifications, newest first, plus the unread badge count

400.description: Malformed cursor

get.summary: The caller's per-category delivery preferences, defaults filled in.

200.description: Every category with its effective preference

patch.summary: Replaces the preferences for the listed categories; unlisted categories keep their value.

200.description: Every category with its preference after the write

400.description: Unknown category, or a duplicated one

post.summary: Marks notifications read — either the listed ids or every unread one.
post.description:
One endpoint rather than two because they are the same operation with a different selector,
and both answer with the resulting unread count so a client never has to guess the badge.

200.description: How many rows changed, and the unread count afterwards

400.description: Neither ids nor all, a malformed id, or too many ids

get.summary: Lists the caller's orgs with their role names.

post.summary: Creates an org; the caller becomes its Owner in the same transaction (decision 19).

get.summary: Public org profile plus the packages this caller may see.
get.description:
Anonymous-reachable: org slugs are not secret ([S-04.b](../../../docs/security.md)) — any
prober who knows one public package name can already tell an existing org base from a
missing one — and an unknown slug answers the same 404 the pub protocol gives. What *is*
protected is the package list, which runs through the same [`SearchView`] as search, so a
non-member sees exactly the org's public, listed packages.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

200.description: Org profile and its visible packages

400.description: Malformed cursor

delete.description:
Refuses with `409 conflict` while the org owns packages. Forcing **archives** instead of
erasing: decision 06 and S-18 keep name claims and version rows forever and both hang off
the org row, so erasing it would un-burn a package name. An archived org loses its members,
invitations, and tokens, and every package it owns goes private + unlisted + discontinued.
Every removed member's sessions are revoked (S-09).

400.description: confirm does not match the slug

409.description: The org still owns packages and force was not set

patch.summary: Updates an org's profile: display name, description, upstream policy (Admin+).
patch.description:
The slug is absent by design — it is the org's virtual registry base (decision 01), and
renaming it would break every `PUB_HOSTED_URL`, lockfile `archive_url`, and CI token
configuration pointing at the old one.

400.description: Invalid name, description, or policy

get.summary: The org's invitations, newest first (Admin+).

post.summary: Sends an invitation (Admin+ and **always** step-up gated — S-06).
post.description:
Unconditionally gated, unlike a direct member add: an invitation reaches an address that
may not have an account yet, so a stolen admin session could otherwise invite an
attacker-controlled mailbox and escalate around the CLI-token publish boundary. Budgeted at
≤20/day/org (S-24).

200.description: Invitation created; the token is shown once

403.description: Below Admin, a role at or above the caller's ceiling (D39), step_up_required, or a domain the S-31 allowlist rejects

429.description: The org's daily invitation budget is spent (S-24)

delete.summary: Revokes a pending invitation (Admin+, step-up — the same gate that created it).

get.summary: The org's members (Admin+).

post.summary:
Adds an existing account as a member (Admin+; step-up for Write and above; the granted
level must sit below the caller's own unless the caller is an Owner — D39).

403.description: Below Admin, a grant at or above the caller's ceiling (D39), or step_up_required for a Write+ grant

404.description: Unknown org, or no verified account with that email

delete.summary:
Removes a member (Admin+; the target's level must sit below a non-Owner caller's own —
D39). Their sessions are revoked (S-09) along with every CLI token they held in this org
(D37).

200.description: Member removed; their sessions (S-09) and their CLI tokens in this org (D37) were revoked

403.description: Below Admin, or a target at or above the caller's ceiling (D39)

409.description: last_owner — the org would be left without an Owner

patch.description:
The gate covers **demotions from** Write+ as well as promotions **to** it: taking somebody's
publish rights away is exactly as consequential as granting them, and a stolen stale admin
session must not be able to lock the real owners out.

200.description: Role changed; the member's sessions were revoked (S-09) along with any org tokens the new level can no longer mint (D37)

403.description: Below Admin, a level at or above the caller's ceiling (D39), or step_up_required

409.description: last_owner — the org would be left without an Owner

get.summary: Package search and browse.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Free text plus filter tags: `format:` `org:` `topic:` `dependency:` `is:` `sort:`,
quoted phrases, and a leading `-` to negate a filter. Unparseable tokens are ignored
and echoed back in `unknown_filters`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page; only valid for the same `sort`.

400.description: Malformed cursor, or one from a different ordering

get.summary: Package detail: metadata, the newest live version, links, flags, counters, README.

404.description: Unknown name, or one this principal may not read (S-04)

get.summary: Packages that depend on this one, from the stored pubspecs.
get.description:
Reverse dependencies are the `dependency:` search filter with the ordering pinned to `name`,
not a second query path — so a package hidden from search is hidden here too, by the same
predicate.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

400.description: Malformed cursor

404.description: Unknown name, or one this principal may not read (S-04)

patch.summary: Replaces a package's mutable options (Write+ in the owning org).
patch.description:
Not step-up gated: these flags are reversible and none of them destroys anything. Flipping
a package to private is the sharpest of them, and it *narrows* access rather than widening
it.

400.description: Unknown visibility value

403.description: Below Write in the owning org

404.description: Unknown name, or one this principal may not read (S-04)

post.summary: Transfers a package to another org (Owner of **both**, step-up — S-06 ownership transfer).
post.description:
Owner on both sides because the operation is two decisions: giving a name away, and taking
responsibility for one. The receiving org inherits the name claim, so its admins are the
ones a shadowing alarm will page from then on (S-17).

400.description: confirm does not match, or the target is the current owner

403.description: Not an Owner of both orgs, or step_up_required

get.summary: A package's versions, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page.

400.description: Malformed cursor

404.description: Unknown name, or one this principal may not read (S-04)

get.summary: One version in full: rendered README and CHANGELOG plus the pubspec document.

404.description: Unknown package or version, or one this principal may not read

delete.summary: Hard-deletes a version (Admin+, step-up, and an explicit confirmation — decision 06).
delete.description:
Three gates rather than one because this is the only operation in the system that destroys
bytes somebody may already depend on: the role (Admin, not Write — publishing and erasing
are different authorities), a fresh second factor (S-06), and a `confirm` field naming
exactly `{name}@{version}`. The tombstone survives, so the number is burned forever (S-18),
and the blob is removed only when no live version still shares its content hash.

200.description: Version hard-deleted; the number stays burned

400.description: confirm does not name this version, or reason is missing

post.summary: Retracts a version (Write+, step-up — S-06).
Restores a retracted version (Write+, step-up).
post.description:
Allowed only inside `registry.unretract_window_days` (default 7 — decision 06). The flag is
a resolution signal that lockfiles and downstream caches have already reacted to, so
flipping it back weeks later would resurrect a version the ecosystem routed around; outside
the window the answer is a `409 conflict` that names the window.

409.description: Not retracted, or past the restore window

get.summary: Trivial app-API echo endpoint proving the envelope contract end-to-end.
Lists the caller's live sessions, most recently seen first, with the current flag (S-10).

post.summary:
Revokes every session of the caller (S-09 revoke-all), the current one included.
**Step-up gated** (S-06): the explicit revoke-all is on the dangerous-action list.

delete.summary:
Revokes one of the caller's sessions (S-09/S-10). A session the caller does not own is
indistinguishable from a nonexistent one: 404 either way (S-04).

get.summary: Lists the caller's tokens: hints, scopes, last-used, expiry — never secrets (S-13).

post.summary:
Mints a CLI/API token. The secret appears in this response and never again (S-13
show-once); at rest only its SHA-256 and a first-8-chars hint survive.
post.description:
Minting `publish` or `admin` scopes is **step-up gated** (S-06): a stolen stale web
session must not escalate around the CLI-token publish boundary. `read`/`retract` mints
stay ungated.

200.description: Minted token — the secret is shown once

403.description: Org role below the requested scopes, or step_up_required for publish/admin scopes

delete.summary:
Revokes one of the caller's tokens — effective everywhere within ≤ 60 s (S-13).
Foreign and unknown ids are both 404 (S-04).

get.summary:
Liveness/readiness probe. Always on, never authenticated (decision 23); orchestrators
poll it, so it must stay cheap — one trivial query per backend.

Archive download — a redirect to a presigned URL where the backend can sign, the bytes
themselves otherwise (decision 10).
get.description:
Retracted versions are served: lockfile-pinned builds must keep working (sharp edge 9).
Tombstoned ones are not: their bytes are gone (decision 06).

200.description: The archive, byte-identical to the upload

307.description: Presigned URL for backends that sign

401.description: Credentials required or rejected; carries WWW-Authenticate

get.summary: Publish step 1 — authorize "may publish *something*", hand back the upload URL.
get.description:
This request carries no package name (docs/protocol.md endpoint 2), so name claims,
package patterns, and duplicate checks are impossible here and belong to finalize. What
*is* checked is everything name-independent: a token, the `publish` scope, the org binding,
and the Write role.

403.description: Token lacks publish scope, org binding, or Write role

post.summary: Publish step 2 — the byte sink: store the archive, answer `204` + `Location`.
post.description:
Deliberately dumb (docs/protocol.md sharp edge 5). The only checks are the ones a dumb sink
still needs: a credential, so the endpoint is not an open blob writer, and the body limit.
The client sends no `Accept` here, so no version negotiation runs either.

requestBody.description: multipart/form-data with the archive in field `file`

204.description: Stored; `Location` points at the finalize URL

400.description: Not a readable multipart body, or no `file` field

403.description: Token lacks publish scope, org binding, or Write role

429.description: The org's S-24 publish budget is spent; carries Retry-After

get.summary: Publish step 3 — run the whole pipeline and answer `200 {"success":…}` or `400 {"error":…}`.

parameters.name: session
parameters.description: Upload session id from the Location header

400.description: Any permanent rejection: bad archive, bad pubspec, duplicate version, expired session

403.description: Wrong credential for this upload, missing scope/role, or a name owned elsewhere

get.summary: Version listing — the endpoint the client re-fetches before every resolve and download.

401.description: Credentials required or rejected; carries WWW-Authenticate

404.description: Unknown name, or one this principal may not read (S-04)

AdminOrgDto.description: One row of the admin org table.

version.description:
Instance settings version — increases on every write, and is what the cross-instance
reconciliation poll compares.

AdminSettingsPatchBody.description: Body of `PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings`: any subset of sections, each replaced wholesale.

runnable_jobs.description: Jobs this instance can run on demand.

settings_version.description: The settings version this instance is serving.

shadowing_active.description: How many of those alarms are unacknowledged.

AdminUserDto.description: One row of the admin user table.

instance_admin.description: Whether the account administers the instance.

actor_id.description: Actor id; `null` for the system actor.

id.description: ULID id — also the pagination cursor.

ip.description: Client IP, when the action came from a request.

metadata.description: Structured before/after context; never contains secrets (S-22).

org_id.description: Org context, when the action is org-scoped.

Backends.description: Configured backend kinds, as selected by config (decision 09).

logo_url.description: Absolute logo URL; empty = the UI's own mark.

primary_color.description: Accent colour; empty = the theme default.

blob.description: The blob store answered a probe.

database.description: The database answered a probe query.

kv.description: The KV store answered a probe.

CountersDto.description:
Instance counters, **scoped to what the caller may see**.

Scoped rather than absolute on purpose: an absolute package count on a public page publishes
the size of every org's private inventory, and an absolute zero on a fully private instance
is a useless dashboard. The same predicate as search, so the numbers always agree with what
a listing returns.

packages.description: Visible packages holding at least one live version.

DownloadsDto.description:
Download counters as of the last rollup (docs/architecture.md `download_stats`).

Deliberately "as of the last rollup", not live: counting a download writes to an in-process
buffer that a background job drains, so these numbers trail reality by up to one flush
interval and must never be used for anything but display.

recent.description: Downloads in the instance's trailing statistics window (30 days by default).

message.description: Human-readable description; never parsed by clients.

count.description: How many matches fall in it.

FacetsDto.description: Facet aggregates over the whole result set, not just this page.

orgs.description: Top owning orgs by match count.

confirm.description:
`"{name}@{version}"`, typed again. The bytes are unrecoverable and the number is burned
forever, so the request has to name exactly what it destroys.

reason.description: Why — recorded in the audit event (S-22). Required.

blob_removed.description:
Whether the archive bytes were removed. `false` means another live version shares the
content hash, so erasing them would break a `pubspec.lock` that pins it.

tombstone.description: Always `true`: the row survives so the number can never be reused (S-18).

backends.description: Which backend kinds this instance is configured with.

checks.description: Live connectivity per backend — each is an actual ping, not an echo of config.

status.description: `"ok"` when every configured backend responds, `"degraded"` otherwise.

version.description:
Server version: the release version injected from the git tag at build time
(decision 18), or the crate version marked `+dev` for non-release builds.
Git metadata is in `pubd --version`.

most_downloaded.description: Most downloaded packages (by all-time count as of the last rollup).

InstanceDto.description: Instance identity for the landing page (decision 17 white-label).

primary_color.description: Accent colour as a CSS colour string; `null` when unset.

public_url.description: Public base URL — what a user puts in `dart pub token add`.

token.description: The token from the invitation email.

role.description: Role granted on acceptance; defaults to `read` (S-06 least privilege).

InvitationCreatedDto.description: Response of creating an invitation: the row plus its show-once token.

token.description:
The single-use token, shown exactly once. Also mailed to the invitee; it is returned
here so an instance with no SMTP configured can still onboard people. Only the holder
of the invited address — verified — can redeem it.

JobRunDto.description: Result of a manual job run.

JobStateDto.description: Durable state of one background job.

lag_seconds.description: Seconds since that success; `null` when it never succeeded (a different alarm).

last_success_at.description: When a run last succeeded — the freshness an operator watches.

phase.description: The job-defined phase its cursor belongs to.

processed.description: How many work items were processed in total.

ListDto_PackageSummaryDto.description: Cursor-paginated list envelope (docs/rules/api.md: cursor pagination only).

cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor; `null` on the last page.

items.description: One package as a search result or listing row — everything a result card renders.

description.description: Description from the newest live version's pubspec.

latest_retracted.description: Whether the **newest** version is retracted (which may not be `latest_version`).

latest_version.description: The version a fresh `pub add` would pick.

published_at.description: When the newest version was published.

replaced_by.description: Suggested replacement; only meaningful while discontinued.

unlisted.description: Whether the package is hidden from discovery.

LoginDto.description:
Response of a sign-in step or refresh.

Two shapes behind one schema: `mfa_required = false` carries the full pair;
`mfa_required = true` carries only `mfa_token` — the client must redeem it at
`POST /api/v1/auth/totp/verify` with a TOTP or recovery code (S-05).

mfa_required.description: Whether a second factor is still outstanding.

refresh_token.description: Opaque refresh token — rotates on every refresh (S-08).

email.description: Verified email of an existing account. Unknown addresses are 404 — invite them instead.

role.description: Role to grant; defaults to `read` (S-06 least privilege).

MemberDto.description: One row of the org members table.

display_name.description: Display name; `"deleted user"` for an anonymized account (S-29).

email.description: Email, when the account still has one.

role.description: The role the user now holds; `null` when the membership was removed.

sessions_revoked.description:
How many of the affected user's sessions this change revoked (S-09). Always `0` for a
pure grant, which cannot be spent by a token issued before it.

tokens_revoked.description:
How many of the affected user's CLI tokens **in this org** the change revoked
(decision 13 addendum, D37): those whose scopes exceed a lowered level, every one of
them on a removal, none on a grant or a raise.

MfaVerifyBody.description:
Body of `POST /api/v1/auth/totp/verify` — exactly one of the two fields.

[`Debug`] is hand-written: codes are live credentials (S-25).

mfa_token.description: The pending-MFA handle from the first-factor response.

NotificationDto.description: One row of the notification feed.

id.description: Notification id — also the pagination cursor and the value to mark read.

org_id.description: Org context, when the event had one.

payload.description: The event document, verbatim — the same shape the SSE stream carried.

read_at.description: When the caller marked it read; `null` = unread.

NotificationFeedDto.description: Response of `GET /api/v1/notifications`: the standard cursor envelope plus the badge count.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation cursor; `null` on the last page.

items.description: Notifications on this page, newest first.

unread.description: Total unread notifications — the badge, independent of this page.

email.description: Whether matching events are also emailed.

in_app.description: Whether matching events appear in the feed.

NotificationPreferencesBody.description: Body of `PATCH /api/v1/notifications/preferences`. Categories left out keep their value.

NotificationPreferencesDto.description: Response of the preferences routes: every category, defaults filled in.

NotificationsReadBody.description: Body of `POST /api/v1/notifications/read`: either specific ids or everything.

ids.description: Notification ids to mark read. Ignored when `all` is set.

marked.description: How many rows this call changed (already-read and foreign ids count for nothing).

unread.description: The unread count afterwards — the new badge value.

code.description: Authorization code from the IdP redirect.

flow_id.description: Flow handle from the start step (server-side state binding, S-01).

state.description: `state` from the IdP redirect — must match the server-side record exactly.

flow_id.description: Flow handle to hold (e.g. sessionStorage) and present at the callback.

data.description: Response of `GET`/`PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings`.

version.description:
Instance settings version — increases on every write, and is what the cross-instance
reconciliation poll compares.

data.description: Response of `GET /api/v1/admin/stats`.

runnable_jobs.description: Jobs this instance can run on demand.

settings_version.description: The settings version this instance is serving.

StreamEventDto.description:
One frame of `GET /api/v1/events`, as it appears in the SSE `data:` field.

A projection, not the domain enum: the stream is a public wire contract the frontend
generates types from, and serializing `DomainEvent` directly would make every future
variant field a silent API change. The common fields are lifted out so a client can route on
them without a per-type match, and `data` carries the whole event document for the cases
that need more.

The full event document (`type`-tagged, snake_case), for clients that need more than
the lifted fields.

`id:` field, so a browser client that uses `EventSource` semantics gets it for free.

package.description: Package name, for the package-lifecycle events.

type.description:

`org.member`, `notification.new`, …).

version.description: Version, for the events that name one.

message.description: Text the CLI prints on a successful publish.
